thesis: A solo coding agent like Claude Code or Codex is a brilliant individual worker locked inside one code repository's sandbox: it only acts when a human tells it to, it has no live reach into the company's production systems, and it has no idea which real customers or dollars a bug is touching. HiveMind is the opposite: a steerable crew of separately-credentialed AI specialists that notices a business problem nobody filed a ticket for (sales just dropped, no error was thrown), then fans out across six real partner systems at once -- Dynatrace, Elastic, GitLab, BigQuery/Fivetran, MongoDB Atlas, Phoenix -- to assemble the whole story a single agent never could: the code bug AND the bad deploy that caused it AND the named paying customers bleeding revenue AND the privacy data that must be scrubbed before any public fix. Crucially it then STOPS and lets a human steer each high-stakes move from a Slack-style war-room, and a separate evaluator process independently re-checks GitLab to prove the fix is real and not a demo trick. The one-line wow your mom gets: "No human noticed the bug -- the AI crew did, found it was costing $21,600 a month and hurting three named customers, hid their private data, drafted the fix as a pull request, and asked a person before shipping. The coding bot on your laptop would never have known to look."

agent_roster.name: Commander
agent_roster.role: Incident Commander + narrator. Writes the pinned plain-English BRIEF card the instant the channel opens (what/impact/severity/who), narrates handoffs ('Detective handed off to LogDiver'), and adjudicates the one staged disagreement or escalates it to the human. Decides and communicates; does NOT fix.
agent_roster.partner: None (template/state-driven; reads OrchestratorState and emits system-authored events). At most one cheap Gemini-Flash call.
agent_roster.why: Directly fixes the #1 user critique ('a channel materializes and you don't know what it's about'). The n=234 'Watching AI Think' study measured that a no-narration flow is rated 'unengaging, minimal effort' -- literally the user's complaint. It maps to the real ICS Incident-Commander role. Built as a thin non-LLM narrator so it costs ~zero against the Vertex per-minute throttle.

agent_roster.name: Detective
agent_roster.role: Lead diagnostician. NL->DQL->Davis->notebook against Dynatrace Grail; emits the root-cause hypothesis + a confidence score (already in InvestigationFinding.confidence) the UI surfaces as calibrated language.
agent_roster.why: Already the fan-out gate (implicated_service drives route_after_detective). Unchanged role; per-scenario Grail seed makes it find a different root cause each time.

agent_roster.name: LogDiver
agent_roster.role: Log forensics. ES|QL over ~5k logs with a LOOKUP JOIN on the deploy registry to blame a specific deploy. Creates the disagreement moment in Scenario 4.
agent_roster.why: Unchanged code. Per-scenario DEPLOYS rows in seed_elastic_deploys.py make it blame a DIFFERENT deploy (ticketing v3.1, fraud-rules, inventory-sync, pos-gateway) instead of always payment-service v2.4.1 -- this is half the gimmick fix.

agent_roster.name: CodeArch
agent_roster.role: Ops Lead. Reads the real repo tree, drafts a minimal patch, opens a REAL merge request as @HiveMind-bot. The action behind the mandatory human approval gate. Gains a 'revert MR' mode for the rollback-vs-patch fork.
agent_roster.why: Mechanism unchanged and grounded by fetch_repo_tree(). We push 5 new real files into the tiny repo so its MR is genuinely different per scenario -- the other half of the gimmick fix. Adding a revert-MR mode (reuses create_branch/create_or_update_file) enables the rollback-vs-patch human decision.

agent_roster.name: CustomerLiaison
agent_roster.role: The headline differentiator. Names affected customers + revenue from live BigQuery, AND fires the right Fivetran depth play per scenario: A) provision a connector, B) run a transformation, C) GDPR column-level PII redaction. Also lends its BigQuery client to two personas (DataAnalyst for the retail mystery, Compliance for the PII gate) to feel like a bigger team without new serial LLM nodes.
agent_roster.why: All three depth plays already exist and are verified (test_liaison_create/transform/redact GREEN) but customer_liaison_node passes an EMPTY context, so they never fire. One line per scenario -- set req.context -- activates them. This is the white space every AI-SRE incumbent admits ('which customers are affected cannot be solved with logs and metrics alone') and NO competitor does data-side GDPR remediation.

agent_roster.name: Scribe
agent_roster.role: Scribe + memory. Writes the postmortem to Atlas AND vector-recalls past incidents ('have we seen this before?') at the START of a run.
agent_roster.why: ColdMemory.recall and related_to already exist (autoEmbed on summary) but are UNUSED on the live path. Wiring recall in surfaces the incident.io signature 'we've seen this before' wow (Scenario 3 remembers a prior region-sync typo) -- a compounding-memory beat a solo agent structurally cannot show.

agent_roster.name: Reviewer
agent_roster.role: Critic / QA authority. approve/revise/escalate with a self-rewriting rubric (flywheel). Gates the whole incident; pairs with the external Evaluator as the verification authority on screen.
agent_roster.why: Unchanged. Already gates every incident in reviewer_node and can revise to any specialist. Its escalation path becomes a war-room card; the external Evaluator's GitLab re-check becomes the on-screen anti-Devin pill.

human_in_loop_protocol:
TODAY there is no human-in-the-loop: run_full runs the LangGraph to END then fires events.complete(), and store.ts line 225 (`if (get().liveChannels[channelId]) return;`) makes composer @mentions die locally with no backend path. We build the round-trip on machinery that already exists -- OrchestratorRunner already uses AsyncRedisSaver keyed by thread_id, and LangGraph's interrupt() + Command(resume=...) persists to exactly that checkpointer.

MECHANISM (small lift): (1) a node calls interrupt({intent payload}); LangGraph snapshots state to Redis and the graph STOPS. (2) Just before interrupting, the node emits a new `decision_request` event over the existing bus (new builder in hivemind/events.py next to status/token/complete) that the war-room renders as an inline approval card. (3) The human clicks a button (or types an @mention answer); the frontend hits a NEW endpoint POST /api/incident/{id}/resume with {decision, edits?, feedback?}. (4) That endpoint calls graph.ainvoke(Command(resume=decision), config={thread_id: incident_id}), resuming from the checkpoint. The existing AGENT_TIMEOUT/shield() machinery already tolerates long pauses. The four canonical LangGraph decisions -- approve / edit / reject-with-feedback / respond -- map 1:1 to the buttons.

THREE MANDATORY PAUSE POINTS (the canonical irreversible / high-blast-radius / novel triggers): (P1) Before CodeArch's MR is opened -> an Intent-Preview card showing the exact one-file diff, the path, the rationale, the confidence, AND the customer/revenue impact Liaison already computed. Buttons: [Approve & open MR] [Edit the fix] [Roll back instead] [Handle it myself]. (P2) Before a Fivetran GDPR PII redaction -> a Compliance card: 'This decline-log export contains customer_id/email (PII). Redact before the public MR? GDPR exposure if not.' Buttons: [Redact & continue] [Skip] [Show columns]. This is the my-mom-says-wow, solo-agent-can't moment. (P3) At the rollback-vs-patch fork (Scenario 4) -> a Decision card with both options costed live by CustomerLiaison ($X/min bleeding). Buttons: [Roll back now] [Patch forward] [Do both].

TWO NON-BLOCKING STEER POINTS: (S1) @mention an agent to dig deeper ('@log_diver check the 14:05 deploy too') -> delivered as Command(resume={human_message}) into that agent's next run; this is incident.io's conversational steering, table stakes everyone has and we don't. (S2) Answer a low-confidence agent's question (also how the staged disagreement reaches the human).

HOW IT FEELS: pills stream live as today. When the graph hits an interrupt, the agent's pill flips to a distinct new state `awaiting_human` with a soft pulse ('paused for you') -- not a spinner, an invitation -- and an approval card appears inline; NOTHING irreversible has happened. The human clicks; an audit line appears ('MR opened -- revert available 15 min' / 'PII redacted: customer_id hashed'); the pill returns to thinking and the graph resumes from the checkpoint. The escalation path (finalize_node escalated=true after N tries) surfaces as its own card: 'Crew tried 3 times and isn't confident -- here's what it found. [Take over] [Send back with a hint].' This is the 'window then door' pattern: observe through a window, open the door only when a decision is genuinely needed.

ui_changes.area: Pinned BRIEF card (top of every incident channel)
ui_changes.change: On channel creation, before any agent runs, the Commander emits a new `brief` event rendered as a sticky card above message-list.tsx. Template: '#inc-260608-payment-declines - SEV-1 - INVESTIGATING / What: card payments declined for legitimate customers since 02:14 UTC / Impact: ~5% of auths failing - 4 Enterprise accounts - ~$21,600/mo at risk / Suspected: payment-service v2.4.1 deploy / On the case: Detective, LogDiver, CodeArch, Liaison, Reviewer.' The channel name itself encodes date+system+symptom. New Channel fields (brief, impactSummary, customersAffected) in lib/types.ts.
ui_changes.why_third_person: Directly answers the user's 'a channel materializes and you don't know what it's about.' This is the 5-second incident-commander brief; many stakeholders read ONLY this line. Today the channel opens with a raw single token, which is the exact failure mode.

ui_changes.area: Live agent REASONING under each bubble
ui_changes.change: Today _stream_summary streams only each agent's final conclusion. Add a one-line 'why I'm doing this' streamed BEFORE the result, and render the existing tool_call status pills with the real tool name (already passed: events.status(..., tool=call.name)) plus a new short tool_result string, in a collapsible Agent-Trace thread. Example surfaced: 'execute_dql -> 412 timeouts on /checkout; incident_log_triage -> blames payment-service v2.4.1.' Expertise-supportive voice.
ui_changes.why_third_person: The n=234 study: visible expertise-supportive reasoning raised Understanding & Trust 71.6 vs 61.7; the no-reasoning control was rated 'unengaging, minimal effort' -- the user's literal complaint. Showing real tool names is Codex's 'receipts/citations, not prose' trust pattern. The measured fix for fire-and-forget.

ui_changes.area: Impact / Decision / Verification right rail (new impact-panel.tsx)
ui_changes.change: A persistent right panel with three stacked sections fed by intermediate customer_report + the complete payload: IMPACT (named customers e.g. CUST-011 $7,500, revenue at risk, segments), DECISION (the active approval card with diff + buttons when paused), VERIFICATION (the external Evaluator pill: 'Verifying MR exists... confirmed by an independent process'). Calibrated-confidence language throughout ('potential avenue' vs 'root cause confirmed').
ui_changes.why_third_person: Keeps the CustomerLiaison revenue wow (the differentiator no incumbent shows) permanently visible instead of buried in the stream. The Evaluator pill is the anti-Devin trust moment -- harness/evaluator.py's _fetch_mr already re-checks GitLab and FAILs a fabricated MR; putting it on screen is the cherry-pick defense Devin lacked.

ui_changes.change: A thin horizontal timeline across the channel header of timestamped beats: 02:14 alert -> 02:15 cause found -> 02:17 fix drafted -> [paused for human] -> 02:19 MR opened, verified. Every scenario video ends on the delta.
ui_changes.why_third_person: The single most legible non-expert wow is a before/after time number (incident.io's own SREcon talk is titled 'From 4 Hours to 8 Minutes'). It makes the whole arc a story a newcomer reads in one glance, and shows WHERE the human steered.

ui_changes.area: Approval cards inline + new awaiting_human pill state (new approval-card.tsx)
ui_changes.change: Render the decision_request event as an inline card (diff on top, impact line, buttons below) whose buttons POST to /api/incident/{id}/resume. Add a new PillState 'awaiting_human' (pulsing 'paused for you'). Wire composer.tsx @mention and these buttons through a new store action respondToAgent(incidentId, decision) instead of the local-only early-return at store.ts line 225.
ui_changes.why_third_person: Makes the run VISIBLY defer to a human -- which is itself the wow ('the AI did all the work then asked a person'). The pulsing pill tells a third person the crew is waiting on them, not hung.

scenarios.title: Brick-and-Mortar Retail: one region's revenue down with flat footfall (the cross-system mystery)
scenarios.business_symptom: Store region 'Midwest-Mall': revenue down 22% week-over-week, but footfall is flat and POS uptime is normal. A business mystery, not an exception -- nothing is 'down.'
scenarios.why_impossible_for_solo_coding_agent: Nothing errored and nothing is technically down. The truth -- an inventory-sync job silently stopped reconciling shelf-vs-system stock for one region, so popular SKUs show 'in stock', never reorder, and quietly stock out -- lives across the sales-by-store warehouse + the sync-job logs + the job config. No single log says 'Midwest-Mall is broken.' This is the purest multi-agent parallel-correlation case and the strongest 'use ALL the agents' scenario. Anchored to phantom inventory: out-of-stocks are a ~$1.2T global problem from system-stock != shelf-stock.

build_order: 1. KILL THE GIMMICK (data + repo, highest ROI, no agent-code changes). Push 5 new real files to the tiny GitLab target repo, each with a planted, inline-commented bug: ticketing-service/pricing-rules.yaml, fraud-rules/velocity.yaml, inventory-service/sync-config.yaml, pos-gateway/capacity.yaml, data-policy/pii-allowlist.yaml (the last is the MR target, not a bug). CodeArch already grounds on fetch_repo_tree() so it will read the right file per scenario. This alone makes every MR genuinely different.

2. PARAMETERIZE THE SEEDS per scenario. Make seed_elastic_deploys.py emit a different culprit deploy (ticketing v3.1, fraud-rules, inventory-sync, pos-gateway) instead of always payment-service v2.4.1; parameterize seed_dynatrace.py Grail logs to each scenario's service/symptom; add a small BigQuery store_sales table for S3 and (if needed) a ticket_orders slice for S1; seed a prior region-sync incident into Atlas so ColdMemory.recall returns it in S3. Replace demo_scenarios.json's one-bug-three-skins with the 5 distinct scenarios.

3. ACTIVATE THE DEPTH PLAYS (one-line plumbing, already-built tools). In customer_liaison_node set req.context per scenario so depth play C fires in S2/S5 and A/B fire in S5. The tools (create_connection/run_transformation/modify_connection_column_config) are already verified GREEN -- they just never receive a context today.

4. WIRE SCRIBE VECTOR RECALL. Call ColdMemory.recall (or related_to) at the start of a run and stream 'have we seen this before?' into the channel -- the method already exists and is unused on the live path. Powers S3's memory beat.

5. BUILD THE HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP ROUND-TRIP (the core new architecture). biggest_risks: Vertex per-minute throttle (~3 min cooldown) makes full 6-agent runs serial and ~2-5 min. Mitigation: keep exactly 6 true serial Gemini nodes -- the 'new agents' (Commander, DataAnalyst, Compliance, SRE-Actions) are thin template narrators or personas/modes of existing agents, NOT new LLM hops. HITL pauses actually HELP by spacing LLM calls across human think-time. Record videos with one fresh fire per session.

Seeding 5 distinct, internally-consistent datasets is the real work, not the code. Each scenario needs Dynatrace Grail logs + an Elastic deploy-registry row + a BigQuery slice that all tell the SAME story and all point at the SAME repo file the planted bug lives in -- exactly the cross-seed coherence the current single-bug setup already has for checkout. Budget time for this; it's where a 'reskin' would sneak back in.

The HITL interrupt()/Command(resume) wire touches the orchestrator's hot path and the Redis checkpointer. A bug here can freeze a run mid-incident. Mitigation: reuse the existing thread_id/AsyncRedisSaver resume path that run_full already exercises; gate interrupts behind a per-scenario flag so a non-HITL run still completes end-to-end; keep the AGENT_TIMEOUT/shield() backstop.

The staged disagreement (S4) must be a GENUINE evidence-grounded conflict, not scripted theater -- a savvy audience punishes the Devin cherry-pick. Mitigation: make LogDiver's surge-blame and CodeArch's config-blame both literally true given the seeded data, so the human is choosing between two valid fixes, not watching a puppet show. The external Evaluator on screen is the honesty backstop.

BigQuery currently only has services checkout/payment-service/search/notifications and 12 customers; S1 (ticketing) and S3 (store regions) need new tables/slices. Mitigation: add a small store_sales table for S3 and extend customer_usage services_used (or a ticket_orders table) for S1 -- small, real additions, not fabrications.

Scenario S5 is non-incident and triggered by a schedule, not the Dynatrace webhook -- there's no scheduled-trigger path today. Mitigation: a simple cron/manual fire that builds a synthetic 'sweep' payload and calls OrchestratorRunner directly (the proactivity is the point; the trigger mechanism can be a script for the demo). Treat S5 as optional/stretch behind the 4 incident scenarios.

Compliance/PII redaction via Fivetran modify_connection_column_config affects a real connector's column config -- a destructive-looking write in a live demo. Mitigation: it's already verified (test_liaison_redact GREEN) and the human approval gate (P2) sits in front of it; demo against the known port_doubting group connector, and keep the redaction reversible/idempotent.
